transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. As you know, the 25-ton overhead crane in Bay 2 has its routine annual inspection scheduled for Friday. We've got eight finished frames staged in the bay already, with four more expected during the week. Before I finalize any decisions around the inspection timing and crane downtime, I want to follow our standard pre-job huddle process. I need maintenance, production scheduling, and EHS to review the work plan so we can make sure we're not creating bottlenecks or safety issues. Let's hear from each of you.

transcript.text: I need to flag something urgent before we go any further. During my inspection this morning, I found that the crane brake lining is at 18% remaining. Our maintenance standard requires immediate removal from service when brake lining drops below 20%. That means the crane needs to come down right now — not Friday. The repair itself is a 6-hour brake replacement, and after that we have to perform a 125% rated-capacity proof-load test before the crane can go back into service. I haven't entered this in the maintenance system yet, but I'm disclosing it here so we can act on it immediately.
